prompt: Which of these belongs to the transport layer rather than the data layer?

choices.text: The tools/call method and its params
choices.why: Methods and params are the data layer.

choices.text: One message per line on standard input and output
choices.why: Right. That is stdio's framing.

choices.text: The error code -32022
choices.why: Error codes are part of the messages.

choices.text: A result's resultType field, which says whether the call completed or needs input
choices.why: Fields of a result are the data layer.

prompt: What makes a JSON-RPC message a notification?

choices.text: A method whose name starts with notifications/
choices.why: The name is a convention; the missing id is the rule.

choices.text: Being sent by the server
choices.why: Clients send notifications too, such as notifications/initialized.

choices.text: It has no id
choices.why: Right. Nobody answers it; raw.py waits for a reply only when there is an id.

choices.text: Its params are empty
choices.why: Params can be present or absent.

prompt: What replaced the handshake in the 2026-07-28 revision?

choices.text: A token the server issues on the first request, which the client must send back afterwards
choices.why: No token is issued; each request stands alone.

choices.text: A cookie set by the server
choices.why: There are no sessions to keep in a cookie.

choices.text: Nothing; versions are no longer checked
choices.why: The server refused 1999-01-01.

choices.text: Every request carries the version and capabilities in _meta
choices.why: Right. Nothing connection-wide needs remembering.

prompt: What do ttlMs and cacheScope on a list result tell the client?

choices.text: Its freshness and its cache scope
choices.why: Right. How long the answer stays fresh (here 0) and whether a shared cache keeps it (here private).

choices.text: How long the server took to answer
choices.why: That would be a timing; ttlMs is a freshness hint.

choices.text: Which tools are private to this client
choices.why: cacheScope is about caches, not about tools.

choices.text: When the server will shut down
choices.why: Nothing in the result says so.

prompt: What is the difference between a protocol error and a tool execution error?

choices.text: There is none; both are JSON-RPC errors
choices.why: A tool execution error is a result with isError.

choices.text: Protocol errors are for the model, tool errors for the developer
choices.why: It is the other way round: isError results are meant for the model.

choices.text: Which part failed: the request, or the tool
choices.why: Right. A JSON-RPC error for the request; a result with isError for the tool, meant to be read and acted on.

choices.text: Protocol errors only happen over HTTP
choices.why: -32022 and -32602 came over stdio.

prompt: How did this SDK answer a call to a tool that does not exist?

choices.why: The specification lists that; the SDK did something else.

choices.text: With a result marked isError, 'Unknown tool: get_ordr'
choices.why: Right. A client should check for both kinds.

choices.text: It closed the connection
choices.why: The connection stayed open.

choices.text: It called get_order instead
choices.why: Nothing was called.

choices.text: Because JSON cannot carry state

choices.text: So that the person cannot read the question

prompt: Over Streamable HTTP, the header that repeats a tools/call's tool name is `___`.

choices.text: Because the server reads only the header
choices.why: It read the body and compared.
